    If one regular hexagon represents 1, draw an area model for \(\dfrac{2}{3}\).

    Construct the desired model. Then \textbf{explain} each step of its construction process. How is the denominator represented in the model? How is the numerator represented? How does each inform the construction process?

    The denominator of 3 tells us to split the whole (represented by a regular hexagon) into 3 equal parts. The numerator of 2 tells us to select 2 of the 3 parts. We show this selection by shading. Thus, we have a model of the fraction 2/3.

    Given the number line below, mark the value \(\dfrac{3}{5}\).

    Construct the desired model. Then \textbf{explain} each step of its construction process. How is the denominator represented in the model? How is the numerator represented? How does each inform the construction process?

    The denominator of 5 tells us to split the whole (represented the distance of 10 spaces between 0 and 1) into 5 equal parts. The numerator of 3 tells us to select 3 of the 5 parts. We show this selection by placing our point 6 spaces to the right of 0. Thus, we have a model of the fraction 3/5.
